# Course Introduction

## Patterns

*What humans do with the language of mathematics is to describe patterns.*

Lynn A. Steen, mathematician 

*All mathematics is is a language that is well tuned, finely honed, to describe patterns*

Brian Greene, physicist


---

## Patterns

*Mathematics is the science of patterns, and nature exploits just about every pattern that there is.*

Ian Stewart, mathematician


*A mathematician, like a painter or poet, is a maker of patterns. If his patterns are more permanent than theirs, it is because they are made with ideas.*

G. H. Hardy, mathematician

---

## Welcome to Math 300

Welcome to Math 300 Discrete Mathematics! I am Prof. Geoffrey Buhl, and I am you instructor for this semester. Buhl rhymes with fuel.

Class Session Goals:

- Meet Classmates and work in small groups.
- Learn about this course and my expectations.
- Work on a first discrete mathematics problem.

---

## Syllabus Activity

1. Take a few minutes to introduce yourselves and share what other
   courses you are taking this semester.

2. As a group, take 10–15 minutes to look over the syllabus and
   formulate four questions your group would like to ask about the course.

3. As a whole class, groups will ask questions and I will answer them.

## Advice from past students

Former student's answer to the question "What advice would you give
students to be successful in this class?" at the end of the semester:


- Start homework early, do it consistently, and redo missed or difficult
problems since homework closely matches exam questions.
- Attend every lecture, pay attention, take clear notes, and ask questions
to fully understand concepts and proofs.


---

## More advice from past students

Former student's answer to the question "What advice would you give
students to be successful in this class?" at the end of the semester:

- Use support resources regularly, including the Learning Resource Center,
office hours, review sessions, and practice exams.
- Form study groups early, collaborate with classmates, and communicate
through group chats or Discord.


---

## Even more advice from past students

Former student's answer to the question "What advice would you give
students to be successful in this class?" at the end of the semester:

- Practice star problems, proofs, and pretests, and build a helpful
formula sheet with key concepts and examples.
- Take advantage of extra credit opportunities and manage your time,
stress, and sleep to stay on track.

## Activity: Worksheet

In small groups, work on the "Tiling with Triominos" worksheet. The
goals of this worksheet are to:

- Experience the challenge of understanding what a question is asking
- Practice the problem solving strategy of drawing pictures.
- Practice the problem solving strategy of working on "Small n" versions
of a general problem.

![Right triomino](triomino.jpg){width=30% fig-align="center"}
